message.content:
Let  
\[
x=\alpha+1,\qquad y=\beta+1.
\]
Then
\[
xy=\alpha\beta+\alpha+\beta+1=-99,
\]
and since \(|\alpha|=|\beta|=M\),
\[
|x-1|=|y-1|=M.
\]
Also \(x\neq 0\), so \(y=-99/x\).

Now compute the equality of squared moduli:
\[
|x-1|^2=\left|\frac{-99}{x}-1\right|^2=\left|\frac{x+99}{x}\right|^2.
\]
Let \(t=|x|^2>0\) and \(S=x+\overline{x}\). Then
\[
t+1-S=\frac{t+99S+9801}{t}.
\]
Multiplying by \(t\),
\[
t^2-tS=t+99S+9801,
\]
so after canceling \(t\),
\[
t^2-9801=S(t+99).
\]
Thus
\[
(t-99)(t+99)=S(t+99).
\]
Since \(t+99>0\), we get
\[
t-99=S.
\]
Therefore
\[
M^2=|x-1|^2=t+1-S=t+1-(t-99)=100.
\]
Hence \(M=10\).

This value is attainable: \(\alpha=-10\), \(\beta=10\) satisfies the original equation and has common modulus \(10\).

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
